 Mariners To Acquire Maikel Garcia
 By Charlie Wright |
 at November 18, 2026 10:31am CDT 
 10:31 am:  Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic reports the final player in the deal is righty L.P. Langevin .
 10:23 am:  Passan reports that right-hander James McArthur and a minor league reliever are headed to Seattle in the trade. It’s a three-for-three swap.
 10:10 am: The Mariners are trading for Royals infielder Maikel Garcia , reports Jeff Passan of ESPN . Right-hander Bryce Miller is among the players going to Kansas City. Ryan Divish of the Seattle Times reports that righty Logan Evans and lefty Jose A. Ferrer are also part of the return.
 Seattle was known to be hunting for an infielder on the left side to pair with Colt Emerson . Kansas City was in the market for pitching help. Both sides accomplished their goals with a blockbuster deal. Garcia was an All-Star and Gold Glove award winner in 2025. Miller will immediately slot into the Royals rotation, with Ferrer potentially taking over as closer.
 Garcia inked a five-year, $57.5MM extension last winter. The deal also includes a $21MM club option with a $3.2MM buyout. It added an extra two years of club control, with the club option factored in. Garcia is set to make $7MM in 2027.
 After serving as a speedy utility option in his first few seasons, Garcia broke out as a critical cog in Kansas City’s lineup in 2025. He slashed .286/.351/.449 with 16 homers and 23 steals as the everyday third baseman. Garcia posted a career-best 120 wRC+ across 666 plate appearances.
 The Royals used Garcia to fill gaps at second base, shortstop, and the outfield early in his career. He played almost exclusively third base in 2025 and had a tremendous year with the glove. Garcia recorded 13 Defensive Runs Saved and 17 Outs Above Average en route to Gold Glove honors.

 Third base is a wasteland in MLB these days, especially young 3B talent, so being able to trade for one should cost a lot. That said, KC got some guys, but noone all that great. Miller has had one good season, and now moves to a less favorable park. Evans stuff, in last year’s Baseball Prospectus write-up, “simply doesn’t miss enough bats at this point to make him anything more than an emergency starter/mop-up reliever” and Ferrar is just a guy, and not worth writing home about. All that said, M. Garcia isn’t great on paper, but he’s at an age that there could still be hope he reverts to something closer to his 2025 season….though the park change doesn’t help him either. All in all, a reasonable trade of complementary pieces.
 Given the shortage of 3B options around baseball (especially AVAILABLE 3B options), I give Seattle the slight nod on this one.
